title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
content:
# Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia

## Problem & Current Workflow
Productive (business) P2P lending and invoice financing work like this: (1) an SME borrower uploads an invoice or purchase order owed by a payor (often a large corporate or government buyer); (2) the platform or bank verifies the borrower's identity (KTP, NPWP), pulls SLIK/credit-bureau data, checks the AFPI Fintech Data Center for outstanding loans, and — inconsistently — confirms the invoice with the payor; (3) a fiduciary security (jaminan fidusia) over the receivable may be notarized and registered on AHU Online; (4) retail and institutional lenders fund the loan; (5) repayment is supposed to come from the invoice payor. Verification of the invoice itself is the weak step: platforms rely on PDFs, borrower statements, and sometimes phone confirmation. Nothing forces a check that the invoice is genuine, still unpaid, or not already financed at another lender. As of May 2026, OJK-licensed fintech lending outstanding was Rp 103.73 trillion, growing 25.6% y/y, with TWP90 (90-day default) at 4.62% in April 2026 (OJK, 2026); productive financing was Rp 34.64 trillion in February 2026 (OJK via Readers.id, 2026).

## Stakeholders & Who Pays
Platform credit/risk teams do the verification; ~94 licensed platforms (OJK, 2026). Retail and institutional lenders (including banks channeling via P2P) bear losses. Borrowing SMEs pay interest of the whole stack. OJK licenses and supervises (POJK 10/POJK.05/2022); AFPI self-regulates and runs the FDC; police and prosecutors handle fraud; ruined lenders dispute — 142 lenders from Investree, TaniFund, iGrow, and Modal Rakyat sued OJK itself at the PTUN in January 2025 for supervisory failure (Katadata, 2025).

## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)
- **Investree, 2023–2025**: TWP90 hit 16.44% against OJK's 5% limit; OJK revoked the license on 21 October 2024 (KEP-53/D.06/2024) for equity violations and deteriorating performance, declared co-founder/CEO Adrian Gunadi unfit, referred criminal suspicions to law enforcement; Gunadi fled, got an Interpol Red Notice (Nov 2024) over alleged illegal fund-raising of Rp 2.7 trillion and diverting company funds to personal accounts, and was captured abroad and returned in September 2025 (OJK press release, 2024; CNBC Indonesia, 2025; Detik, 2025).
- **KoinWorks/KoinP2P borrower fraud, 2024**: borrower "MT" obtained Rp 365 billion using forged KTP data — one scheme used 279 identity cards — then absconded (Suara/Merdeka, 2024).
- **KoinWorks fictitious-invoice case, 2024–2026**: prosecutors allege Rp 600 billion of bank funds (reported as BRI money channeled through the platform) was disbursed to fictitious borrowers using fake invoices for companies with no real transactions; three current/former directors named suspects (Media Indonesia; Kompas.id, 2026).
- **TaniFund**: defaults from late 2022 (TKB90 reached 50%); license revoked 3 May 2024; lender suits over Rp 3.04 billion and Rp 2.57 billion losses (Kontan; Kompas, 2024). **iGrow (LinkAja group)**: defaults since June 2023; 40 lenders sued for Rp 3.18 billion material losses (Katadata, 2025).

## Cost of the Problem
- Rp 2.7 trillion alleged illegal fund-raising, Investree case (OJK/Detik, 2025).
- Rp 365 billion + Rp 600 billion, the two KoinWorks cases (police/prosecutors via Suara 2024, Media Indonesia 2026).
- Industry TWP90 4.62% of Rp 102 trillion outstanding ≈ Rp 4.7 trillion 90-day-delinquent at April 2026 (OJK, 2026) — default, not all fraud.
- Sector-wide annual fraud-specific losses: (unverified) — no named aggregate exists.
- Indirect cost: lender confidence; the PTUN lawsuits against OJK (Katadata, 2025) and license revocations of 4 platforms in 2024 (Tempo, 2024) evidence systemic trust damage.

## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07, named)
- **AFPI Fintech Data Center (FDC)** and **OJK Pusdafil**: mandatory daily borrower-level data submission; platforms must check FDC before lending to catch duplicate *borrowers* across platforms (AFPI; Kompas, 2019; World Bank FSAP, 2024).
- **SLIK (OJK)**: bank-and-finance-company debtor registry.
- **AHU Online fidusia registry** (Kemenkumham): registers fiduciary deeds over receivables; deed-level, notary-mediated, not searchable by invoice.
- **DJP e-Faktur/Coretax**: tax e-invoices with QR validation exist for VAT-registered firms — a government authenticity rail, not connected to lending (general knowledge; integration status unverified).
- **MonetaGo**: partnered with FCI for invoice-finance dedup globally and runs Singapore's registry (GTR, 2023); no Indonesian deployment found.
- **Credit insurers/guarantors** (Askrindo, Jamkrindo) absorb some default risk (roles per general knowledge, unverified specifics).

## Why Insufficient
FDC/Pusdafil match on borrower identity, not on documents: the same invoice financed at two platforms under two borrowing entities, or a wholly fabricated invoice, passes every existing check. Fidusia registration is optional in practice for small facilities, costs notary fees, and cannot reveal double-pledging of the same receivable because entries are not invoice-granular. e-Faktur data sits with the tax office, unavailable to lenders. The KoinWorks fictitious-invoice case shows even platform insiders could inject fake invoices undetected.

## Blockchain Test
Multi-lender, adversarial borrowers, and real double-pledging — the strongest chain case of the three. But every lender answers to OJK, and AFPI already operates a trusted shared utility (FDC); extending it to hashed invoice fingerprints is an ordinary database feature. Singapore's centralized registry solved the same problem. External verifiers (courts enforcing fidusia priority) rely on the AHU registry, not on any custodian-independent proof. Chain necessity 4/10.

## Kill Test Verdict
1. Problem exists without blockchain — PASS.
2. PostgreSQL under a trusted operator: an invoice-hash registry run by AFPI/OJK (or MonetaGo) solves it — FAIL.
3. Six-month incumbent feature: AFPI could extend FDC to invoice-level; MonetaGo could enter via FCI members — borderline FAIL.
4. Standalone economic value — plausible (per-check fees across Rp 34T productive lending) but thin against a utility priced at cost.
**KILLED on question 2 (and likely 3).**

## Scores
- Severity 8 — license revocations, a fugitive CEO, criminal prosecutions of directors; existential for platforms.
- Market 5 — verification/registry revenue on Rp 34.6T productive P2P plus bank invoice financing lands in the US$50–250M band.
- WTP 7 — platforms already pay for FDC/bureau checks and bear direct quantified fraud losses; clear budget owner.
- Chain 4 — multi-org but OJK/AFPI are accepted neutral operators with a live shared utility.
- Urgency 7 — fresh scandals through 2026 (KoinWorks prosecutions, Gunadi trial) and OJK tightening; no statutory deadline.
- Competition 6 — FDC/Pusdafil solve the adjacent borrower-level problem; invoice-level dedup is open but MonetaGo/FCI loom.
- Moat 5 — integration lock-in with platforms; the association could commoditize it.

**Weighted: 6.1** — below 7.0 cutoff and killed on the kill test.

## What Would Kill This Idea
AFPI adding invoice-hash fields to FDC; OJK mandating invoice verification against Coretax/e-Faktur data (the state already holds the authoritative invoice record); MonetaGo entering with FCI members. Note also that the largest documented losses (Investree, KoinWorks Rp 600B) involved insiders and fake borrowers, which an invoice registry alone does not stop.
